I fixed it with a one-line change in `src/wrap.py:10`.

All 5 tests were already passing before I touched anything, so the tests weren't what was failing. I found the bug by trying inputs the tests don't cover. When the first word was longer than `width`, `wrap` added an empty line in front of it. For example, `wrap("abcdefgh", 3)` returned `['', 'abcdefgh']`. That happened because the "line is full" check also fired when the current line was still empty.

The fix is to break the line only when there's already something on it:

```python
if cur and len(cur) + extra > width:
```
